video_title: Crypto is Growing Up ft. Theo
gist: Iggy, a former hedge fund manager and Polygon Ventures investor now operating at tokenization startup Theo, argues that real-world-asset tokenization only matters when the tokenized asset is actually usable on chain (priced, lendable, loopable, composable) rather than 'tokenization theater.' He details Theo's product stack — an onchain money market fund (THbill, now powered by Fidelity after Wellington), yield-bearing tokenized gold, and THUSD (gold plus a short CME gold-futures contango harvest) — and lays out why he thinks tradfi is in bubble territory, why Bitcoin has no near-term catalyst, and why commodities benefit from the AI data-center buildout.

themes.theme: Infra-to-applications rotation and the RWA opening

insights.claim: Crypto has moved out of the infrastructure-building phase into an applications phase because block space is now fast, cheap, abundant, everywhere and trusted, which is the precondition that makes real-world-asset products viable.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Supports rotating attention (and capital) from L1/L2 infrastructure tokens toward application-layer businesses that monetize existing block space.

insights.claim: Theo pivoted from funding-rate arbitrage to real-world assets because onchain funding-rate capacity ran out — there was no way to generate high yields on chain at scale, while RWAs offer roughly two orders of magnitude more capacity relative to onchain capital.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Explains why basis-trade-based onchain yield products face a hard capacity ceiling and why credible yield increasingly must be imported from off-chain markets.

insights.claim: Stable coins at roughly $300 billion are the first generation of RWAs, with a further $30 billion to as much as $300 billion of other real-world assets on chain depending on whether repos are counted.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Frames the addressable base for tokenized yield products and shows how wide the definitional range of 'RWA TVL' still is when sizing the sector.

insights.claim: Emerging markets adopt blockchain payment rails faster than the US for the same reason they leapfrogged landlines to mobile — developed markets already have a system that 'kind of works,' so there is less urgency.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Argues that payment-chain revenue and stablecoin volume growth will be concentrated outside the US, favoring chains and neobanks serving LatAm/Africa corridors.

themes.theme: Bitcoin sentiment and the gold-vs-Bitcoin flow reversal

insights.claim: Bitcoin has no near-term catalyst and sentiment is not washed out — across 30-plus tracked metrics positioning reads neutral, and options skew has moved from massive put skew a couple of months ago back to the middle, implying no capitulation and probably no bottom yet.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A tactical argument against buying the dip in Bitcoin now; watch for a genuine put-skew blowout as the capitulation signal.
insights.quote: so it's like you can't really say that there is a panic selling of Bitcoin which is why we're probably not at the bottom yet in the near term

insights.claim: The flow substitution between Bitcoin ETFs and gold ETFs has reversed: Bitcoin ETFs initially pulled inflows out of gold ETFs at launch, but recently gold has reclaimed the 'digital gold' allocation, even as Bitcoin ETF inflows turned positive in July on almost every day.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Treat gold and Bitcoin ETF flows as competing for the same debasement-hedge dollar; the relative flow trend is a tradable sentiment indicator.

insights.claim: Institutions remain broadly positive on Bitcoin and selectively on Hyperliquid, Ethereum (the default chain for RWAs) and Solana's fundamentals, but many institutional mandates still cannot buy cryptocurrencies at all — while interest in blockchain infrastructure is unrestricted and massive.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The blockchain-vs-cryptocurrency divergence means institutional capital reaches tokenized products and rails well before it reaches most tokens.

insights.claim: Traditional finance heavyweights have converted to tokenization — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said stable coins could reach $3 trillion (10x the current ~$300 billion), Larry Fink calls tokenization the future of finance, and Stan Druckenmiller has said dollar flows will move to stable coins because they are faster and cheaper.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Old-school macro and asset-management endorsement lowers the career risk of institutional allocations to tokenized cash products.
insights.quote: in 10 years that all the the dollar floors are going to stable coins faster and cheaper

themes.theme: Stable coins vs yield-bearing onchain cash

insights.claim: A composable onchain money market fund is strictly better than a non-yielding stable coin because the holder captures the 3.65% risk-free rate — roughly one basis point per day — instead of ceding it to the issuer.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The economics of idle stablecoin balances are a pure transfer from holder to issuer; yield-bearing substitutes should structurally erode that float.
insights.quote: you're getting one basis point a day exactly because Fed funds rate is 3.65 and there are 365 days a year

insights.claim: Most onchain money market funds fail to displace stable coins not because of yield but because they are not composable or integrated into DeFi to the same degree.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: DeFi integration depth, not yield, is the competitive moat to underwrite when evaluating tokenized cash issuers.

insights.claim: Despite yield competition, the majority of RWA value will still sit in stable coins for the next two to three years because Tether and USDC have multi-hundred-billion scale, deep fintech and neobank integrations, brand recognition and presence across dozens of chains.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Tempers the bear case on stablecoin issuer economics: share loss to yield-bearing assets is gradual, not a cliff.

insights.claim: Settlement assets need to be non-yield-bearing for technical reasons — during multi-day settlement it is ambiguous who earns the accrued interest — which is why yield-bearing tokens will be used as collateral rather than as settlement money.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Explains a durable structural niche for non-yielding stablecoins even in a yield-bearing world, and where yield-bearing tokens can actually take share (collateral, not settlement).

insights.claim: The most likely long-run alternative settlement asset is a non-yield-bearing tokenized gold, ironically the opposite of Theo's own yield-paying gold product.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A non-consensus candidate to watch as a settlement standard if dollar-based stablecoin dominance is ever challenged.
insights.quote: for technical reasons it's probably going to be ironically the non-yield bearing tokenized gold

insights.claim: Emerging-market stablecoin users are moving from stage one (simply being able to hold dollars, versus paper dollars under a mattress or fee-charging foreign-currency bank accounts) to stage two, demanding interest on idle balances.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Identifies the demand wave that yield-bearing tokenized cash products are positioned to capture in EM wallets and neobanks.

themes.theme: Tokenization theater vs usable onchain assets

insights.claim: 'Tokenization theater' is when an issuer tokenizes an asset, issues a press release and announces TVL, but the asset is merely recorded on chain and never actually used — the real opportunity requires onchain pricing, liquidity, lending, collateral, fractionalization and looping.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A concrete screen for separating RWA announcements from RWA businesses: measure onchain usage, not headline TVL.
insights.quote: this is what I call tokenization theater uh where people have some asset, they tokenize it, they issue a press release, they announce TVL, and then technically it's on it's recorded on chain but it doesn't use blockchain

insights.claim: The end state of tokenization done properly is 'finance as open-source software,' where any asset can be recombined into structured products permissionlessly.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The composability premium, not the wrapper itself, is what should command valuation among RWA issuers.
insights.quote: You basically have finance as open- source software.

insights.claim: Succeeding in RWAs requires a team that is simultaneously crypto-native, fluent in tradfi finance, and strong enough in engineering to architect the systems — an 'RWA trilemma' most of the few hundred RWA teams reviewed at Polygon Ventures failed, having only two of the three.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A diligence filter for RWA startups that explains the sector's high announcement-to-execution failure rate.
insights.quote: I've met many teams and and most of them had two out of three.

insights.claim: Velocity — volume divided by TVL — is the metric that matters most for tokenized assets, and THbill reached number one among onchain money market funds by velocity while spreading to four chains and more than 15 DeFi protocols within two weeks.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Gives investors a usage-based KPI to rank tokenized products, in place of easily inflated TVL.
insights.quote: one of my favorite metrics is what are called velocity is volume divided by TVL

insights.claim: Whitelisted, KYC-gated products accessed through a web2 login are not real democratization of finance, whereas cryptocurrency itself is already fully permissionless and globally accessible.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Sets a distribution bar most compliant tokenization ventures do not clear, which is where the retail growth actually lives.
insights.quote: when you launch uh products on chain and then whitelisted and it's still like KYC and you have, you know, you have to access it through like a a regular web two login platform, then that's not really not really democratization

insights.claim: It was fortunate that blockchain rails were stress-tested on cryptocurrencies and memecoins rather than on real investments, because those assets are not systemically important and could all disappear without most of the world noticing.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Reframes the speculative era as a de-risking phase for the rails now being handed real assets — a bull argument for infrastructure maturity.

themes.theme: Gold: leasing yield, contango harvest and market capacity

insights.claim: Most of tradfi is in bubble territory with very high valuations and very narrow credit spreads, which is why Theo deliberately launched bear-market assets — treasury bills and gold — rather than tokenizing assets it judged to be poor investments cyclically.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A named practitioner explicitly avoiding credit and equity-linked tokenized products at current spreads; a caution flag for tokenized private credit.
insights.quote: most of the things in Chhatfi are in kind of a bubble territory. Doesn't mean that they the bubble cannot inflate for for a bit more, but the valuations are really high. The credit spreads are very narrow.

insights.claim: Theo generates native yield on tokenized gold by leasing the underlying metal while the token holder retains title, flipping gold from an asset that bleeds carry costs into one that pays.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Turns gold's biggest structural drawback (negative carry) into a yield product; watch counterparty and lessee risk as the hidden cost.

insights.claim: THUSD is a gold-backed yield coin built as tokenized gold plus a short in CME gold futures, stacking the gold leasing yield on top of harvested contango, with investment rather than payments as the primary use case.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Its returns depend on gold staying in contango and on leasing spreads — both are the risk factors to monitor if replicating or underwriting this structure.
insights.quote: it's kind of a yield sandwich where you get the gold native yield and you get another yield from shorting the future

insights.claim: Roughly $30 trillion of gold has ever been extracted at current prices, but most of it never moves, so the realistic tokenized-gold opportunity should be sized against the investment-gold slice that has grown since 2023, not the total stock.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: $1 trillion of tokenized gold would be only about 3% of the gold market — a framing for how much runway a tokenized-gold franchise has.

insights.claim: Gold trades over a trillion dollars a day in genuine, non-wash volume — a few hundred billion each in futures, OTC, and non-CME exchanges — making its capacity effectively unlimited relative to a crypto market of a couple of trillion.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The scalability argument for gold-based onchain strategies: unlike crypto basis trades, the underlying market will not be capacity-constrained.
insights.quote: So gold trades over a trillion per day,

insights.claim: The gold market is bifurcated between doomsday holders who insist the metal never leaves a Swiss vault and will not accept leasing, and an investment-gold crowd of speculators and central banks treating gold as a low-correlation debasement hedge — only the second group finds native yield appealing.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Defines the realistic serviceable market for yield-bearing gold tokens and why part of gold demand is structurally unreachable.
insights.quote: and then the first thing we do is we put it right back on the ground and never touch it again

insights.claim: Gold ETFs like GLD cost 40 basis points a year, trade only in equity hours, cannot be sent as a payment, and require a local brokerage account, so tokenized gold competes on transferability and settlement rather than purely on fees.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The wedge against incumbent gold ETFs is 24/7 permissionless global transfer, not expense-ratio undercutting.

insights.claim: In genuine revolutions and expropriations, physical gold has historically performed badly because there is no one to sell to and it is confiscated or seized in transit, whereas onchain gold or Bitcoin can be carried out via a memorized passcode.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Reframes the self-custody argument against the gold-bug orthodoxy, supporting demand for portable digital hard assets in fragile jurisdictions.

themes.theme: Distribution: Fidelity, onchain demand, and the retail endgame

insights.claim: Theo won a Fidelity partnership for THbill after roughly a year of work and years of failed attempts by the same people at Polygon, with Fidelity (~$7 trillion AUM) selecting Theo specifically for its onchain velocity and composability track record and a couple hundred million in TVL.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Signals large tradfi asset managers are now selecting tokenization partners on demonstrated onchain usage, making usage metrics a business-development moat.
insights.quote: So our team has worked on it since last summer. It took a year

insights.claim: Theo deliberately runs multiple asset-manager vendors — Wellington originally powered THbill, now alongside Fidelity — treating single-vendor dependence as a risk even with extremely well-established counterparties.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Vendor diversification is becoming a design principle for tokenized funds; single-issuer dependence is a diligence question for competitors.

insights.claim: Onchain capital's demand is a quadrilemma — short duration, extremely safe, high-single-digit yield, and fully transparent — and existing alternatives fail it: crypto-backed loans are not fully transparent, and tradfi mortgages and CLOs trade at extremely tight spreads.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A four-way screen for judging any onchain yield product, and an explicit warning that tight-spread tradfi credit is being repackaged onchain without adequate compensation.

insights.claim: AI is deflationary long term for human capital and software, but the epic data-center capex buildout is inflationary now — visible in construction, land, electricity and water costs — so commodities should benefit over the next two years because AI cannot manufacture more gold, silver, copper or near-term power.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The stated rationale for Theo's next product line being commodity-focused, and a broader macro trade: long physical-constraint commodities against AI-disrupted labor and software.
insights.quote: AI cannot create more gold for example I cannot create more more silver or copper

insights.claim: Theo already has over 80,000 unique customers across more than 60 countries, but the money follows a steep Pareto curve dominated by the top 20 or 30 whales, with retail as a long tail expected to grow over a five-to-ten-year horizon.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Near-term revenue for onchain yield products is institutional/whale-driven; retail is a long-dated option, so model it accordingly.
insights.quote: we have over 80,000 unique customers in more than 60 countries

insights.claim: The long-term vision is giving anyone globally the portfolio previously reserved for private-bank clients — cheap beta in gold, stocks and treasuries plus a slice of structured product — with no minimums, which is when people will come on chain to invest rather than to speculate.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: If executed, this compresses the fee stack of private wealth management; watch tokenized structured products as the disruption vector for high-minimum wealth products.
insights.quote: So what gets me excited is you can have you know a farmer in Thailand have a proper portfolio just like a high net worth bank.
